claim.markdown_says: NOTE   In the example: / '          PROGRAM-ID.  A.' / '             ...' / '          PROGRAM-ID.  B.' / '          ...' / '             PROGRAM-ID.  C.' / (blank line) / '             ...' / '             END PROGRAM C.' / '          END PROGRAM B.' / '       END PROGRAM A.'
claim.why_it_matters: This example exists solely to illustrate containment nesting (the very next paragraph reads 'Program B is directly contained in Program A; Program C is directly contained in Program B'). In the markdown 'PROGRAM-ID.  B.' sits at the SAME column as 'PROGRAM-ID.  A.' (col 10), so B reads as a sibling of A rather than nested inside it, and 'END PROGRAM A.' is outdented to col 7, left of its own PROGRAM-ID. The indentation is the information content of this figure and it is scrambled.

verdict.reasoning: CONFIRMED by independent ink-column measurement of the 300 dpi render (spec_p285.png, printed page 255), not by trusting the claim's numbers. Per-text-band minimum dark-pixel x: 'PROGRAM-ID.  A.' 557, '...' 636, 'PROGRAM-ID.  B.' 630, '...' 636, 'PROGRAM-ID.  C.' 702, '...' 708, 'END PROGRAM C.' 700, 'END PROGRAM B.' 628, 'END PROGRAM A.' 555. The 2 px spread between an 'E' and a 'P' left edge is glyph side-bearing noise, and a monospace period's ink sits ~11 px (~0.42 cell, cell width ~26.6 px derived from the ink spans of the 14- and 15-character lines) inside its cell, so the printed columns resolve unambiguously into exactly THREE left edges: level 0 = {PROGRAM-ID. A., END PROGRAM A.}, level 1 = {'...'#1, PROGRAM-ID. B., '...'#2, END PROGRAM B.}, level 2 = {PROGRAM-ID. C., '...'#3, END PROGRAM C.}. Step between levels is a uniform ~73/72 px. Each END marker aligns with its own PROGRAM-ID. The markdown's equivalence classes are DIFFERENT, not merely shifted: {END PROGRAM A.} alone at col 7, {PROGRAM-ID. A., PROGRAM-ID. B., '...'#2, END PROGRAM B.} at col 10, {'...'#1, PROGRAM-ID. C., '...'#3, END PROGRAM C.} at col 13. A got merged into B's level and END PROGRAM A. was pushed out to a level of its own. This is not an isomorphic re-indentation, so it cannot be dismissed as whitespace formatting - the refutation grounds I checked all fail: no text is missing or reflowed (every token is present), this is not page-break furniture, line wrapping or hyphenation (the figure is inside a fenced monospace block whose entire semantic payload IS the column layout), and the claim misquotes neither source (the markdown quote matches byte-for-byte, and the claim's pdf x-values are within 3 px of my measurements). I also verified the defect is in the committed transcription and not an extraction artifact: specs/ISO_COBOL.md at offset ~694963 contains the identical corrupted block. The transcribed figure is additionally self-contradictory - 'END PROGRAM A.' printed to the LEFT of its own 'PROGRAM-ID.  A.' is a layout that cannot represent any nesting - and it contradicts the immediately following prose by placing B at A's column. Mitigating but not exculpating: that following prose states the containment relationships explicitly in words, so a human reader is not deprived of the information; the loss is confined to the figure.
verdict.corrected_description: Real, and the claim's core is accurate, but it under-reports the damage by two further defects. (1) The claim frames the error as 'B at A's column and END A outdented'; the fuller statement is that the markdown regroups the figure's THREE printed indent levels into a different partition - PDF levels are {A, END A} / {'...', B, '...', END B} / {C, '...', END C}, whereas the markdown yields {END A} / {A, B, '...'#2, END B} / {'...'#1, C, '...'#3, END C}. (2) The two '...' lines in the A/B region are printed at the SAME column in the PDF (both at B's level: ink 636 and 636), but the markdown puts them at col 13 and col 10 respectively. (3) The markdown inserts a blank line between 'PROGRAM-ID.  C.' and the following '...' that does not exist in the PDF: the printed figure has a uniform 53 px line pitch across all 10 lines (NOTE 2176, then 2229, 2282, 2335, 2387, 2440, 2493, 2545, 2598, 2651), i.e. exactly 9 consecutive non-blank lines from 'PROGRAM-ID.  A.' to 'END PROGRAM A.' with no gap. Also worth recording for whoever re-bakes this figure: the PDF's per-level indent step is a proportional ~73 px, about 2.75 monospace cells, NOT a whole character count, so no character-exact transcription exists - the faithful rendering is a consistent whole-space step (3 spaces) that preserves the relative level grouping, e.g. A at col 10, then '...'/B/'...' at col 13, then C/'...'/END C at col 16, END B back at col 13, END A back at col 10.
